subject: maths
title: Frequency Tables & Charts
welcome_lead: Turn raw numbers into clear tables and charts. See the patterns hiding in data.
meta_desc: Master frequency tables, pictograms and bar charts in this KS3 adventure.
final_note: Brilliant! You can now display data clearly.

concepts.def: How many times a value occurs.
Table showing values and their counts.
Vertical marks to count, grouped in fives.
Chart using icons to represent quantities.
Chart with bars of height equal to frequency.
A line with a scale on a chart.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Multiply each value by its frequency, sum, then divide by total frequency.

Example: values 1, 2, 3 with frequencies 2, 3, 5. Sum = 1×2 + 2×3 + 3×5 = 23. Total freq = 10. Mean = 2.3.

Each bar height shows the frequency of that category.

Make sure the y-axis scale is clearly labelled and starts at 0.

options: Frequency of categories
Only one value

A set quantity
A single item

mcqs.q: On a bar chart showing the number of pets, the bar for 'cat' has height 7. What does the 7 mean?
options: Cats are the seventh most popular pet.
Seven people (or items) in the survey chose 'cat' — frequency is the count.
Seven cats are owned by the people in total.
